assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory turned two-dimensional critical phenomena into an exactly solvable, classifiable problem: scale invariance becomes conformal invariance, with central charge, operator content and universality classes fixed by symmetry. It is a clean, general mechanism that reaches statistical mechanics, string theory and condensed matter, which is the kind of universality I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: The decisive 1984 structure (infinite-dimensional Virasoro symmetry, minimal models) is credited to Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov, but Belavin is not among the supplied names. Within the supplied strings, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov are the core theorists, and Cardy is a fair third for finite-size scaling, boundary CFT and the application to statistical systems. Fridkin-style or Friedan-Qiu-Shenker contributions are not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Mature and decades-old, with extensive confirmation from exact lattice solutions, numerics and experiments on 2D critical systems. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Omission of Belavin from the supplied names leaves the attribution of the original BPZ result incomplete.
Whether the committee regards this as physics for a prize or as mathematical physics.
Experimental confirmation is indirect and mostly through universality classes and exponents.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gives a controlled, exact-in-infinite-dimensions treatment of strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and the coexistence of local moments and quasiparticles. It has become the standard computational framework for correlated materials (DMFT plus electronic-structure methods). It is a conceptually transparent mean-field idea in the statistical-physics tradition.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a quantum impurity problem and the self-consistent scheme. Metzner is not in the supplied names, and Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell also had early roles. Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar can support a reasonable three-person prize, though the early limit-of-large-dimension step makes it partly imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than three decades of use and quantitative agreement for Mott physics and several materials. Its success on real materials is mixed, depending on approximations.
uncertainties: Credit for the infinite-dimension limit (Metzner) is outside the supplied names.
Accuracy for finite-dimensional real materials and for non-local correlations is limited.
Whether the committee sees it as technique versus discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a minimal nonlinear stochastic growth model that defines a universality class with exactly known exponents and distributions linked to Tracy-Widom statistics from random-matrix theory. Its reach extends from interface growth to directed polymers, turbulent liquid crystals and quantum systems. It is a prime example of a simple universal mechanism, close to my own field of interest.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 paper by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang is the origin, but Parisi is not among the supplied names (and is already a laureate). Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments provided the clearest experimental confirmation of universal distributions. A fair prize would likely centre on Kardar and Zhang, possibly with an exact-solution or experimental contributor; Sasamoto, Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and Prähofer-Spohn are not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Theoretically well established, with decisive experimental confirmation arriving only since about 2010. This is mature enough, but the attribution picture is complicated by the exact-solution mathematics.
uncertainties: Omission of Parisi and of the mathematicians who obtained exact solutions complicates a fair credit split.
Experimental realisations are limited and few systems show clean KPZ scaling.
Whether the exact-solution progress is better treated as a separate discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene shows flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity arising from a simple geometric tuning parameter. It opened moiré quantum matter and 'twistronics' as a broad field, and a simple continuum model captures the essential mechanism, which appeals to me.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states. The supplied triple fits theory and experiment well. Cao and others co-authored the key experiments but are not supplied, and Kim and Dean also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Young (2018), but replicated in many groups and quickly broadened to other moiré systems. The origin of the superconductivity is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled; timing is possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit to the first-author experimentalists and other groups is outside the supplied names.
Prize timing could be premature relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new classification of band structures by topology, with protected edge states and a robust experimental signature. It is an influential conceptual advance that connects topology to measurable transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator, with Molenkamp's group giving the HgTe experimental confirmation after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore, and the 3D materials work (Hasan, Zhang), are not in the supplied names, so the credit is incomplete and contested. Compared with B012 this entry is the cleaner theory-plus-experiment trio.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over fifteen years, with broad follow-on work. Practical applications remain limited, but the scientific concept is robust.
uncertainties: Credit around BHZ, Fu-Kane-Mele 3D and Hasan's ARPES work is outside the supplied names.
Overlaps heavily with another candidate on the longlist, which is a fragmented-credit risk.
The 2016 prize already covered topological phases, so novelty relative to that is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the final missing piece of the Standard Model and showed a decades-long experimental programme carried through. Its significance is high, although the theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013.
assessment.attribution: The discovery came from large collaborations, and the decisive leadership roles include the spokespersons and the original proposers. Gianotti and Della Negra/Virdee/Jenni are plausible, but a three-person limit forces awkward choices and risks excluding Jenni; the individual scientific origin of the discovery is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed, with measurements of couplings continuing; recognition would be timely or late by now, although the 2013 prize already took the main credit.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals in huge collaborations is arbitrary.
Possible institutional reluctance since the 2013 prize recognised the theory.
I lack the detailed credit history for the experiment leadership and cannot verify it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time reversal of acoustic and wave fields and wavefront shaping to focus light through strongly scattering media show that multiple scattering can be controlled instead of merely endured. The ideas draw on random-matrix and transmission-eigenchannel theory, so they fit my own area. They underlie imaging in complex media.
assessment.attribution: Fink pioneered time-reversal mirrors for acoustics, and Vellekoop and Mosk demonstrated optical wavefront shaping through opaque media in 2007. The three names form a plausible trio, but the optical contribution and the acoustic contribution are somewhat different discoveries; Dorokhov-Mello-Pereyra-Kumar transmission eigenchannel theory is not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Established in both acoustics and optics with many experiments, but practical impact on imaging is still developing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery, with acoustic and optical parts perhaps needing different recognition.
Lasting impact on biomedical imaging is still unfolding.
Theoretical roots in mesoscopic transport are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled atoms and ions as quantum processors and simulators demonstrated programmable quantum control with proposals for trapped-ion gates and simulation. It is a major platform for quantum information, linking many-body physics and computing.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate in 1995, and Blatt's group realised major experimental implementations; Bloch is central to the optical-lattice simulation side, which I leave out because of the three-person limit. Wineland, who shares ion-trap credit, is already a laureate. A pairing of Cirac-Zoller with an ion-trap experimentalist is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across many groups, although the field remains in rapid development, and the recent 2022 and 2025 prizes touched neighbouring quantum-information themes.
uncertainties: Dropping Bloch separates the ion and optical-lattice sides of a compound candidate.
Overlap with recent quantum-information prizes may lower priority.
Practical quantum advantage is still unproven.
